FROM PLUG-IN TO PEACE OF MIND

Three steps. A clearer picture.

A quick controller check before your next session.

01

Connect your gamepad

Plug in a USB data cable or pair through your device’s Bluetooth settings. Keep this page in focus and press a controller button.

02

Put every input to work

Press the D-pad, face buttons and bumpers. Squeeze both triggers, rotate each analog stick, then release them to check the center.

03

Understand the results

Look for missing inputs or movement at rest. Run a drift sample and download a JSON report to compare with a later test.

ONE WORKSPACE. MANY CONTROLLERS.

Bring your favorite controller.

PadLab reads the browser’s Gamepad API. Support depends on your controller, operating system, connection and browser. A recognized standard mapping gives the clearest results.

GOOD QUESTIONS. CLEAR ANSWERS.

A little more clarity.

What an online controller tester can tell you.

How does this online gamepad tester work?

PadLab reads controller states exposed by your browser’s Gamepad API and displays button values and analog axes. The page refreshes readings with the browser’s animation loop. You don’t need an account or an extension.

Can I test a PS5, PS4 or Xbox controller?

Yes, when your browser and operating system expose it as a gamepad. DualSense, DualShock 4 and Xbox controllers often use the standard browser layout. The diagram uses Xbox-style position labels; PlayStation equivalents appear in the button list. Unmapped devices show numbered raw inputs instead.

Does a nonzero stick value mean my controller is faulty?

Not necessarily. Small center offsets and noise can be normal. Compare the resting reading with the deadzone used by your game. Our three-second test reports mean and peak radial offset; it is an observation, not a hardware pass/fail certification.

Does changing the deadzone here calibrate my controller?

No. The slider changes the shaded reference circle in this tester. It does not rewrite firmware, calibrate hardware or change a game’s settings. Use your manufacturer’s supported calibration utility when available.

Can this measure input lag or polling rate?

It cannot measure true end-to-end input latency or USB polling frequency. Browser frame scheduling and gamepad data updates are different from hardware polling. PadLab intentionally avoids presenting those numbers as a latency benchmark.

Why is the vibration button unavailable?

Vibration requires an actuator exposed by the browser. Some browser, controller and connection combinations provide inputs but no haptic support. A disabled vibration button alone does not indicate broken motors.

Is my controller data stored or sent anywhere?

PadLab’s tester processes controller inputs locally and keeps session readings in memory. It sends no controller readings to a server. Exporting creates a JSON file on your device. Hosting providers may process ordinary web request logs.

Good games start with good inputs.
